findings.title: The deployed workflow never provisions the required profile
findings.evidence: The workflow checks out, installs, migrates, and runs without creating profile.yaml or reading any profile secret. profile.yaml is ignored and absent from tracked files, while the production CLI unconditionally loads it before constructing the pipeline.
findings.consequence: Every scheduled or manually dispatched run exits with Profile not found after migration, so the deployed pipeline never collects jobs or processes pending Telegram actions.
findings.correction: Store the approved profile in a protected GitHub secret or equivalent deployment input, materialize profile.yaml with restrictive permissions before jobpilot run, and document that required deployment value without committing the profile.

findings.title: Missing optional Actions values override defaults with invalid empty strings
findings.evidence: The workflow always exports defaulted settings from secrets/vars. Undefined Actions values expand to empty strings; a narrow Settings construction check failed validation for empty MAIL_PROVIDER, MIN_SCORE, DAILY_APPLICATION_LIMIT, and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE instead of applying their code defaults.
findings.consequence: The documented minimal deployment cannot start unless the operator defines values that the guide says are optional and defaulted.
findings.correction: Omit defaulted environment keys when unset or provide explicit non-empty workflow fallbacks, use Actions variables for non-sensitive settings where appropriate, and make the required/optional documentation match the workflow.

findings.title: Required native-PDF CI verification has no execution evidence
findings.evidence: The Phase 9 commit records 384 passing tests but 9 WeasyPrint skips. The only workflow installs native libraries but neither installs dev dependencies nor runs pytest, ruff, or mypy, so no CI path executes the tests whose marker intentionally skips only outside CI.
findings.consequence: There is no required evidence that the deployment image renders both language PDFs and preserves ATS header order; a native-library or rendering failure can reach the PR undetected.
findings.correction: Add a CI verification job/workflow that installs native and dev dependencies and runs the required gate, then provide a successful run where the WeasyPrint tests execute rather than skip.

findings.title: Architecture and deployment docs overstate accepted idempotency guarantees
findings.evidence: The Phase 9 docs promise every-stage idempotency, exactly-once Telegram processing, harmless crash recovery, and resume-safe long polling. ADR-011/012 explicitly retain windows that can lose an owner action, duplicate proposal artifacts, exceed the daily limit, resend after ambiguous mail transport, or duplicate a manual application after a partial DB failure.
findings.consequence: An operator can treat retries, crashes, or a long-polling migration as fully safe even though accepted failure paths can lose actions or duplicate externally visible work.
findings.correction: Preserve the approved deferred trade-offs, but scope the docs to normal-path idempotency, disclose and link the ADR-011/012 crash windows, and remove exactly-once/resume-safe guarantees until the durable outbox work exists.
